arcadiaGuide.title: Arcadia Methodology Guide
arcadiaGuide.description: Learn about diagram types and elements in each Arcadia layer.

OEB.label: Operational Entity Breakdown
OEB.desc: A hierarchical decomposition of operational entities (organizations, users, external systems) that participate in missions.
OEB.purpose: Identify and structure all actors/entities involved in the operational context before defining their activities.
OEB.contains: Operational Entities, Operational Actors, Composition relationships
OEB.usedFor: Understanding the organizational structure and stakeholders

OAB.label: Operational Activity Diagram
OAB.desc: A hierarchical tree of operational activities showing what needs to be done at the operational level.
OAB.purpose: Decompose high-level missions into concrete operational activities that can be assigned to entities.
OAB.usedFor: Defining what the operational stakeholders need to accomplish

OPD.label: Operational Activity Interaction Blank
OPD.desc: Shows the interactions between operational activities — how activities exchange information and trigger each other.
OPD.purpose: Define interactions between operational activities with data exchanges between them.
OPD.contains: Operational Activities, Operational Exchanges, Functional Chains
OPD.usedFor: Modeling operational workflows and information flows

OCD.label: Operational Capability Blank
OCD.desc: Groups operational activities into capabilities — high-level services the operation needs to provide.
OCD.purpose: Define what the operation must be capable of achieving, similar to use cases.
OCD.contains: Operational Capabilities, Involvement Links, Operational Exchanges
OCD.usedFor: Defining operational capabilities and use-case-like scenarios

OIS.label: Operational Activity Scenario
OIS.desc: A sequence diagram showing how operational entities interact over time to achieve a specific capability.
OIS.purpose: Define operational scenarios and validate that the operational architecture supports required missions.
OIS.usedFor: Validating operational flows through scenario-based analysis

OAAB.label: Operational Architecture Blank
OAAB.desc: The overall operational architecture showing entities, actors, activities, and capabilities in one view.
OAAB.purpose: Give a complete operational picture: who does what, and which capabilities are involved.
OAAB.contains: Operational Entities, Operational Actors, Operational Activities, Operational Capabilities, Exchanges, Involvement Links
OAAB.usedFor: Communicating the full operational architecture at a glance

CSA.label: Context System Actors
CSA.desc: The system under study surrounded by the actors it interacts with.
CSA.purpose: Define the system boundary and identify all external actors and their exchanges with the system.
CSA.usedFor: Establishing the system context before functional decomposition

SAB.label: System Architecture Blank
SAB.desc: The main architecture diagram showing system functions allocated to the system and its actors.
SAB.purpose: Define the system boundary, identify system functions, and show how the system interacts with its actors.
SAB.contains: System, System Actors, System Functions, Functional Allocations, Functional Exchanges
SAB.usedFor: Defining system functional architecture and actor interactions

SDFB.label: System Data Flow Blank
SDFB.desc: Focuses on the data flows between system functions without showing the allocation to components.
SDFB.purpose: Analyze functional dependencies and data exchanges at the system level.
SDFB.contains: System Functions, Functional Exchanges, Function Ports
SDFB.usedFor: Analyzing functional data flows and interfaces

SCD.label: Mission Capability Blank
SCD.desc: Groups system functions into mission capabilities — what the system must be able to do.
SCD.purpose: Define system-level capabilities and validate against operational needs.
SCD.contains: System Capabilities, Involvement Links, Functional Chains
SCD.usedFor: Defining system capabilities aligned with operational needs

SFB.label: System Function Breakdown
SFB.desc: A hierarchical tree of system functions showing the functional decomposition of the system.
SFB.purpose: Decompose system-level functions into finer-grained functions.
SFB.usedFor: Structuring system functions before dataflow analysis

SS.label: Functional Scenario
SS.desc: A sequence diagram showing how system functions interact to fulfill a capability.
SS.purpose: Define system-level scenarios and validate functional chains.
SS.usedFor: Validating system behavior through scenario-based analysis

LAB.label: Logical Architecture Blank
LAB.desc: Shows the logical component breakdown — how the system is decomposed into logical building blocks.
LAB.purpose: Define the system's logical architecture independent of implementation choices.
LAB.contains: Logical Components, Logical Actors, Logical Functions, Function Allocations, Logical Exchanges, Interfaces
LAB.usedFor: Designing the logical building blocks of the system

LDFB.label: Logical Dataflow Breakdown
LDFB.desc: Focuses on data flows between logical functions without showing component allocation.
LDFB.purpose: Analyze functional dependencies at the logical architecture level.
LDFB.contains: Logical Functions, Logical Exchanges, Function Ports
LDFB.usedFor: Analyzing logical data flows and function interfaces

LCB.label: Logical Component Breakdown
LCB.desc: Hierarchical decomposition of logical components — showing the sub-component structure.
LCB.purpose: Define the hierarchical structure of logical components.
LCB.usedFor: Organizing logical components into a hierarchy

LFB.label: Logical Function Breakdown
LFB.desc: A hierarchical tree of logical functions showing the functional decomposition of logical components.
LFB.purpose: Decompose logical functions inherited from system analysis.
LFB.usedFor: Structuring logical functions before dataflow analysis

LS.label: Functional Scenario
LS.desc: A sequence diagram showing how logical components interact to fulfill a function.
LS.purpose: Validate logical architecture through scenario-based analysis.

PAB.label: Physical Architecture Blank
PAB.desc: The final architecture showing physical components, nodes, and their allocations.
PAB.purpose: Define the physical implementation architecture ready for development.
PAB.contains: Physical Components, Physical Nodes, Physical Functions, Physical Actors, Exchanges, Links

PDFB.label: Physical Dataflow Blank
PDFB.desc: Focuses on data flows between physical functions without showing component allocation.
PDFB.purpose: Analyze functional dependencies at the physical architecture level.
PDFB.contains: Physical Functions, Physical Exchanges, Function Ports
PDFB.usedFor: Analyzing physical data flows and function interfaces

PCB.label: Physical Component Breakdown
PCB.desc: Hierarchical decomposition of physical components — showing the implementation sub-component structure.
PCB.purpose: Define the hierarchical structure of physical components for development.
PCB.usedFor: Organizing physical components into a development hierarchy

PFB.label: Physical Function Breakdown
PFB.desc: A hierarchical tree of physical functions showing the implementation-level functional decomposition.
PFB.purpose: Decompose physical functions for detailed development.
PFB.usedFor: Structuring physical functions before dataflow analysis

PS.label: Functional Scenario Diagram
PS.desc: A sequence diagram showing how physical components interact to fulfill a function.
PS.purpose: Validate physical architecture through scenario-based analysis.

Mission.label: Mission
Mission.desc: A high-level goal or objective that the operation aims to achieve.
Mission.purpose: Define the top-level mission that drives all operational activities.
Mission.example: Air traffic control, Border surveillance, Emergency response

OperationalEntity.label: Operational Entity
OperationalEntity.desc: An organization, unit, or resource that participates in operations.
OperationalEntity.purpose: Identify organizational units that carry out operational activities.
OperationalEntity.example: Command center, Field team, Analysis unit

OperationalActor.label: Operational Actor
OperationalActor.desc: A human user or external system that interacts with the operation.
OperationalActor.purpose: Identify external actors (users, other systems) that interact with the operation.

OperationalActivity.label: Operational Activity
OperationalActivity.desc: A task or action performed at the operational level.
OperationalActivity.purpose: Define what needs to be done operationally.
OperationalActivity.example: Track targets, Generate reports, Coordinate teams

OperationalCapability.label: Operational Capability
OperationalCapability.desc: A high-level capability the operation must provide, similar to a use case.
OperationalCapability.purpose: Group activities into capabilities for requirements traceability.
OperationalCapability.example: Target detection, Situation awareness, Command & control

OperationalProcess.label: Operational Process
OperationalProcess.desc: An ordered sequence of operational activities forming a complete workflow.
OperationalProcess.example: Target engagement process, Alert handling process

System.label: System
System.desc: The system under study — the main subject of the architecture.
System.purpose: Define the system boundary and its interaction with actors.
System.example: Radar system, Navigation system, Communication system

SystemActor.label: System Actor
SystemActor.desc: An external system or user that interacts with the system.
SystemActor.purpose: Identify external entities that provide inputs or consume outputs.
SystemActor.example: Operator console, External sensor, Data network

SystemFunction.label: System Function
SystemFunction.desc: A function the system must perform to satisfy operational needs.
SystemFunction.purpose: Define what the system does at the functional level.
SystemFunction.example: Detect targets, Track objects, Display information

SystemCapability.label: System Capability
SystemCapability.desc: A high-level capability the system must provide.
SystemCapability.purpose: Group system functions into capabilities for traceability.

SystemComponent.label: System Component
SystemComponent.desc: A major subsystem or component of the system.
SystemComponent.purpose: Initial system decomposition before logical architecture.
SystemComponent.example: Sensor subsystem, Processing unit, Display module

FunctionPort.label: Function Port
FunctionPort.desc: An input or output point on a function through which data flows.
FunctionPort.purpose: Define precise interfaces for function inputs/outputs.
FunctionPort.example: Target data input, Alert output, Status port

LogicalComponent.label: Logical Component
LogicalComponent.desc: A logical building block of the system — independent of implementation choices.
LogicalComponent.purpose: Decompose the system into logical parts that carry major design decisions.
LogicalComponent.example: Detection module, Tracking module, Display module

LogicalActor.label: Logical Actor
LogicalActor.desc: An external entity at the logical architecture level.
LogicalActor.purpose: Identify external interactions at the logical level.

LogicalFunction.label: Logical Function
LogicalFunction.desc: A function at the logical architecture level.
LogicalFunction.purpose: Define the functional behavior of logical components.
LogicalFunction.example: Process sensor data, Generate alerts, Manage communications

PhysicalComponent.label: Physical Component
PhysicalComponent.desc: A concrete implementation unit — ready for development.
PhysicalComponent.purpose: Define the physical components that will be developed or procured.
PhysicalComponent.example: Software module, Hardware board, Firmware package

PhysicalNode.label: Physical Node
PhysicalNode.desc: A physical resource (hardware, server, device) that hosts components.

PhysicalFunction.label: Physical Function
PhysicalFunction.desc: A function at the physical implementation level.
PhysicalFunction.purpose: Define the detailed functional behavior for development.
PhysicalFunction.example: Parse TCP packets, Render GUI, Store to database

PhysicalActor.label: Physical Actor
PhysicalActor.desc: An external entity at the physical architecture level.
PhysicalActor.purpose: Identify external interactions at the physical level.
PhysicalActor.example: External API, Legacy system, Human operator
